newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian government approves KPN's TNT bid.
newsitem.headline: Australian government approves KPN's TNT bid.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it had approved Dutch postal and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV's (KPN) takeover bid for Australian transport group TNT Ltd.

"The Treasurer has, under foreign investment policy, decided to raise no objections to a proposal by KPN (Australia) Ltd to acquire 100 percent of the issued shares in TNT Ltd by way of a takeover scheme," the Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) said in a statement.
The FIRB said proposals in the general freight transport sector were normally approved unless they raised issues that were believed to be against the national interest.
KPN's friendly bid, announced earlier in October, values TNT at A$2.45 a share or A$2.0 billion.
The European Commission is also investigating KPN's bid on the grounds that it may fall under the bloc's merger rules which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions.
The Commission has until the beginning of November to approve the acquisition or start an in-depth four-month inquiry if concerned about its effect on competition.
TNT shares closed steady at A$2.43 on Thursday.
